auth.notes: Account login in the app; session expiry forces re-login. Device registration is an account-scoped POST under users/{uuid}/product_registration. Not mapped further — none of it is on the local-control path.

data_leaves_device: Product registration record (device model/serial attached to the owner's account) — sent by the phone app, only on the stock registration route
Subscription entitlement state (server-side, via an external billing provider) — checked by the app, never by the firmware
cloud.failure_mode: Nothing breaks on the device. Unlock, all intensity/mode/cooling control and the Pro removal mode are computable and writable offline; the cloud only records the registration for warranty bookkeeping and serves the subscription entitlement the stock app uses to gate its own UI. A total FOREO cloud shutdown leaves a replacement client fully functional, and leaves even the stock app able to drive an already-activated device offline.
cloud.notes: Monetization is a server-side subscription bought via an in-app web flow; the app has no in-app-purchase store integration. The subscription gates the app's "Pro" removal-mode UI for the Peach 2 family, but enforcement is app-side only: if the device reports Pro mode while no subscription is active, the stock app writes Basic mode back to the device. The firmware accepts 0AD0 06 with no credential. See `protocol_details.paywall`.
cloud.vendor_service: FOREO For You cloud (account, product-registration bookkeeping, subscription entitlement)

identity.notes: The security-access and activation writes both take bytes of the device's own BLE MAC, so the address is load-bearing for this protocol, not just an identity key. Whether a factory-locked unit advertises under the same names is unverified (the app finds it, so presumably yes) — see `remaining_unknowns`.

device.name: FOREO Peach 2 IPL hair removal
device.notes:
Mains-powered IPL (intense pulsed light) hair-removal device with BLE, Telink-based chipset, companion app FOREO For You. One spec covers the Peach 2 family — Peach 2, Peach 2 go, Peach 2 Pro MAX, Peach 2 Duo — which share one code path in the app and differ in command dialect (see `protocol_details.dialect_selection`) and in which UI modes the app exposes. Optical output up to 7.3 J/cm² with firmware skin-contact and eye-safety interlocks; intensity levels 0–5 over BLE (the hardware buttons expose five levels per the vendor manual, the app six).
The device ships LOCKED: per the vendor manual it will not turn on until "registered" from the app. The registration the firmware actually checks is a BLE activation write to characteristic 0A20 whose payload is derived purely from the device's own BLE MAC address (see `protocol_details.activation`) — the vendor cloud call the stock app performs first feeds nothing into those bytes. A replacement client can therefore activate a brand-new unit with zero network access.
Custom 16-bit UUIDs on the standard Bluetooth base (0000xxxx-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb). No pairing/bonding at any point (the app never bonds), no MTU negotiation on the Peach connect path — 20-byte writes suffice. No command framing: writes are raw opcode || payload, answers are read back from the command characteristic.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The device advertises whenever powered and accepts a bare connection; there is no pairing mode to enter. Whether a factory-LOCKED unit advertises identically is unverified (the app finds locked units, so presumably yes).

exclusivity.notes: Typical Telink peripherals accept one central at a time, but nothing in the app code establishes it for this device; treat single_connection as likely, not known.
exclusivity.recovery: No bond exists to clear. If a connection stalls, close the vendor app (a single-connection peripheral would otherwise hold the link) and reconnect — the security-access write is required again on every connect.

pairing.notes: No link-layer pairing exists on this device — the app never bonds, and characteristics are readable/writable on a bare connection. What looks like security lives entirely above the link layer and is per-connection: the security-access write (01 A1 <last 3 MAC bytes>) to 0A10, required after every service discovery before the device answers commands, and the one-time activation write to 0A20. Neither involves a secret: both derive from the device's own BLE MAC, which any scanning client already holds. Confidence medium: the never-bonds behaviour is consistent through the app's BLE layer, but nothing here has been tried against hardware.

unpair.notes: Nothing to unpair: the app never bonds and the device stores no bond, so moving to a new client needs no reset and no forget-device step.

issued_to_client: Nothing. No keys, tokens or bonds are issued in either setup route; the cloud route's account session lives entirely in the phone app.
stored_on_device: Activation state derived from the device BLE MAC (written once to 0A20, idempotent)

factory_reset.description: Nobody has established a reset procedure for the Peach 2. The activation write is idempotent and is re-run by the stock app on every connect, so 'resetting' is not part of the normal ownership flow at all: a second-hand unit is adopted by simply connecting and activating it again. Do not guess a procedure on an IPL device — the skin-contact and eye-safety interlocks make improvised button sequences a poor idea. Listed as `unknown` rather than `false` because nothing proves one does not exist.
factory_reset.effect: Not established. No factory-reset procedure was found in the app or in the manual text examined. What a reset would clear is likewise unestablished; the activation state (0A20) and the wake-up flag (0A30) are the only persisted device settings this protocol writes.

methods.description: Scan for a PEACH*/PEACH 2 advertisement, connect (no bonding), write the security-access handshake, then activate: read 0A20 and, if its first byte is 00, write 01 02 <8-byte chipId> where chipId is the keyless permutation of the device's BLE MAC documented under `protocol_details.activation`. Finally enable wake-up on 0A30. Idempotent — safe to run on every connect, as the stock app does.
methods.name: Offline BLE activation (no account, no network)

steps.action: Plug in and scan for a local name starting PEACH (PEACH2, PEACH 2, PEACH™ 2, PEACH2GO, PEACH2ProMAX).
steps.expect: Advertisement with one of the family local names.

steps.action: Write security access: 01 A1 <MAC[3]> <MAC[4]> <MAC[5]> to characteristic 0A10 (last three bytes of the device's own BLE MAC).
steps.expect: Write accepted; retried up to 3 times by the stock app. The device does not answer other commands before this.

steps.action: Read SW revision (2A28) — the device is ready; the value also selects the command dialect.
Read 0A20; if the value starts with byte 00, write 01 02 <chipId(MAC)> (see protocol_details.activation).
steps.expect: Device unlocked; activation persists across power cycles.

steps.action: Read 0A30; unless the value starts with 01, write 01 (wake-up enabled).

cloud.local_alternative: The primary method above: the activation write is computable offline from the device's BLE MAC, so the cloud registration is optional end to end.

methods.description: The vendor flow: sign into a FOREO account in the app, which POSTs a product registration to the vendor cloud and then performs exactly the BLE activation above. The server call is warranty bookkeeping — none of its response feeds the unlock bytes — so this route adds an account and a network dependency without adding anything the firmware requires. Kept as documentation of what the stock app does, and the only route that records the unit under the owner's warranty account.
methods.name: Stock FOREO For You app registration

setup.notes: Nothing to provision — no network, no account. The one gate is the ship-lock: a factory-fresh Peach 2 refuses to operate until a client performs the BLE activation below. The stock app routes that through a FOREO account and a server registration call, but the firmware checks nothing the server returns — the activation payload derives from the device's own BLE MAC — so the offline route is primary. Confidence medium: read from the decompiled app, corroborated in its behaviour claims by the vendor manual, not replayed on hardware.

rejoin.notes: There is no network to rejoin and no bond to move: a new phone just scans, connects, writes the security-access handshake and (idempotent) activation, and drives the device. Nothing on the old phone needs clearing.

testing.notes: No hardware on the bench. All protocol facts were recovered by static analysis of the FOREO For You app 4.4.1 (559); nothing has been replayed against a Peach-family device. The vendor manual corroborates the ship-locked behaviour and the registration requirement.

artifacts.description: Static analysis of the FOREO For You app (2026-08). Source of every protocol fact here: the GATT map and the characteristic-by-UUID resolution, the command opcode table and dialect switch, the security-access handshake, the MAC-derived activation (chipId) algorithm, and the app-side-only subscription enforcement. Also establishes the negative findings: no bonding anywhere on the Peach path, no MTU negotiation, and no in-app-purchase store integration.

FOREO Peach 2 user manual (vendor-hosted, linked in helpful_urls). Corroborates the ship-locked behaviour and the registration requirement, and documents five hardware-button intensity levels versus the app's six.

evidence.open_questions: Everything this spec still owes hardware is itemised in `remaining_unknowns`; the shortest summary is that one service discovery and one connect against a real unit would confirm the containing service UUIDs, the locked-unit advertising behaviour, and the unpinned read-back layouts in a single session.

helpful_urls.description: Vendor-hosted online manual for the Peach 2. Corroborates the ship-locked behaviour and the in-app registration requirement this spec's activation flow replaces, and the five hardware-button intensity levels vs the six app levels.
helpful_urls.title: FOREO PEACH 2 full user manual

helpful_urls.description: The companion app analysed for this spec (package com.foreo.foreoapp; analysed at 4.4.1 / versionCode 559 — the store listing always shows the current release).
helpful_urls.title: FOREO For You on Google Play

covers: Offline activation (unlock) of a factory-fresh unit — chipId derived from the device's BLE MAC, written to 0A20
Removal mode Basic/Pro set/read (0AD0/0BD0 on new firmware; 0AA2/0BA2 flash-mode bytes on old firmware) — Pro accepted by the firmware unconditionally
Serial number (0A05), chip ID (0A07), SW revision (2A28), battery level (2A19)
Temperature-enable and head/body NTC threshold opcodes (0AB2/0AB4/0AB5 families; payload layouts unpinned — see remaining_unknowns)
not_covered: OTA firmware update — a trigger write (0A08) and the TI OAD service are present in the app, but no image-fetch or transfer flow was traced, and whether the current app can OTA a Peach at all is unconfirmed
Firing flashes from the app is not a BLE operation on this device family in the flows traced — flashing is hardware-triggered against the skin-contact interlock
local_access.summary: Fully local by design: BLE is the only radio, and the complete control surface — including the ship-lock activation that the vendor UI presents as requiring an account — is reachable from any BLE host with no network at all.

activation.chip_id_algorithm:
chipId is a fixed, keyless permutation of the 6-byte BLE MAC (m0 m1 m2 m3 m4 m5, in the usual printed order). Let b = [m5, m4, m3, 0x00, 0x00, m2, m1, m0]. Then the 8 output bytes are (all arithmetic mod 256):

  out[0] = (b[2] & 0x0F) | (b[7] & 0xF0)
  out[1] = (b[5] & 0x0F) | (b[1] & 0xF0)
  out[2] = (b[7] & 0x0F) + (0xF0 - (b[6] & 0xF0))
  out[3] = 0xFF - b[6]
  out[4] = b[5] + 1
  out[5] = (b[1] & 0x0F) + (0xF0 - (b[2] & 0xF0))
  out[6] = (b[0] & 0x0F) | (b[5] & 0xF0)
  out[7] = (b[6] & 0x0F) | (b[0] & 0xF0)

No key, no nonce, no server input — pure MAC arithmetic. `scripts/test_foreo_peach2_spec.py` transcribes this algorithm and asserts the vectors below.
activation.description: Run after every connect: (1) security access — write 01 A1 <MAC[3]> <MAC[4]> <MAC[5]> to 0A10 (retried up to 3x by the stock app); (2) read SW revision 2A28; (3) only on a locked/factory unit — read 0A20, and if its first byte is 00 write 01 02 <8-byte chipId>; (4) read 0A30, and unless its first byte is 01 write 01. Steps 3–4 are idempotent and the stock app re-runs them on every connect.

test_vectors.description: Documentation MAC 00:11:22:33:44:55-style placeholder (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF) — identifies no real unit. A client whose chipId(MAC) does not reproduce these bytes has mis-transcribed the algorithm.

vectors.step: chipId (payload of the 01 02 … activation write to 0A20)

command_protocol.framing: No framing: no header, length or checksum. Writes to FFF1 are raw `opcode || payload`. First byte 0A = write/set, 0B = read/query; second byte = sub-opcode.
command_protocol.query_model: Write `0B xx` to FFF1, then READ FFF1 back and parse the returned bytes. A read-back starting with FF FF FF FF means the device was busy; the app retries up to 5 times. Every write is verified by the same read-back.
command_protocol.read_back_formats: Only partially recovered: intensity is the first byte of the 0B01 read-back; removal mode >= 6 means Pro (0BD0). Read-back layouts for 0BC4 (new cooling), 0BA2, 0BB2/0BB4/0BB5 and 0BD1 are not pinned — see `remaining_unknowns`.

dialect_selection.description: Two command dialects exist. Peach 2 go, Peach 2 Pro MAX and Peach 2 Duo always use the NEW dialect. A plain Peach 2 uses the OLD dialect when the last character of its SW revision string (2A28) is in a–c, otherwise the new dialect. Old vs new differs in removal/flash mode (0AA2 flash-mode bytes vs 0AD0 removal mode) and cooling (0AC0 vs 0AC4, 0BC0 vs 0BC4 0007).
dialect_selection.verification_note: Read from the app's dialect-switch logic; suffixes beyond a–c are an edge case called out in remaining_unknowns.

paywall.enforcement: App-side only. If the device reports Pro mode while no subscription is active, the stock app writes Basic mode (0AD0 01) back to the device. The firmware accepts the Pro-mode command (0AD0 06) unconditionally — a replacement client writes it directly and nothing on the device checks anything. The same app-side-only pattern gates features on other FOREO devices in the same app. Intensity levels 0–5 and Basic mode are NOT paywalled. Note the UI distinction: the Basic/Pro mode switch is shown for Peach 2 go / Pro MAX always and for a plain Peach 2 on new firmware (SW revision not ending in a–g); it is hidden on Peach 2 Duo. 'Peach 2 Pro MAX' is a separate hardware SKU, not this software mode.
paywall.mechanism: Server-side subscription (via an external billing provider), bought through an in-app web flow — the app has no in-app-purchase store integration. Entitlement is fetched from the vendor API, cached locally and checked in the UI.

remaining_unknowns: Containing GATT service UUIDs: FFF1 is hypothesized under FFF0 and the 0Axx security/activation block's service is unknown — the app resolves everything by characteristic enumeration; confirm with one service discovery on hardware
Whether a factory-locked unit advertises under the same PEACH* names and answers the security-access write and 0A20 read immediately, or after a first-connect delay
Read-back layouts for 0BD0/0BC4 (new cooling), 0BA2, 0BB2/0BB4/0BB5, 0BD1, and the value map for the 0AC4 new-firmware cooling write
Payload layouts for the 0AB2/0AB4/0AB5/0AD1 set opcodes (only the opcodes were recovered)
Dialect edge cases: SW-revision suffixes beyond a–c on a plain Peach 2 (the app also uses 'not ending in a–g' in one UI gate — the exact suffix sets need hardware reads)
OTA: the 0A08 trigger payload, the image-fetch path on the vendor CDN, and whether app 4.4.1 can OTA a Peach at all
Whether the peripheral accepts only one central at a time (likely for the chipset, not established)
FOREO Bear 2 (microcurrent, same app) appears to share the activation + subscription pattern per code structure — follow-up target if a unit is acquired

get_cooling.description: Read cooling level; 0BC0 on old firmware, 0BC4 0007 on new.

get_intensity.description: Read IPL intensity; the level is the first byte of the FFF1 read-back.

get_removal_mode.description: Read removal mode; a read-back value >= 6 means Pro.

set_body_ntc_threshold.description: Body-NTC threshold set. Payload layout not recovered — only the 0AB5 opcode is known.

set_cooling.description: Set cooling/fan level. Opcode 0AC4 on new firmware (value via a firmware-specific map that was not recovered — see `remaining_unknowns`), 0AC0 on old firmware, where 0AC0 0A is auto-fan.

value.notes: Value-to-level map is firmware-specific and not recovered; old dialect uses opcode C0 with 0x0A = auto-fan.

set_flash_mode.description: OLD-firmware flash mode; the mode byte is repeated five times (Basic = 02 x5, Pro = 03 x5, Face = 01 x5). New firmware uses set_removal_mode_* instead — see `protocol_details.dialect_selection`.

set_flash_voltage_table.description: Flash voltage table set. Payload layout not recovered — only the 0AD1 opcode is known.

set_head_ntc_threshold.description: Head-NTC (temperature) threshold set. Payload layout not recovered — only the 0AB4 opcode is known.

set_intensity.description: Set IPL intensity level, 0–5 (six levels; the hardware buttons expose five per the vendor manual).

set_removal_mode_pro.description: New-firmware removal mode: Pro. This is the paywalled mode the stock app gates behind a subscription — the firmware accepts the command unconditionally, with no credential.

set_temperature_enable.description: Temperature-enable set. Payload layout not recovered — only the 0AB2 opcode is known.

characteristics.name: Command channel
characteristics.notes: All Peach commands are written here and all answers read back from the same characteristic. First byte 0A = write/set, 0B = read/query; second byte = sub-opcode. Dialect selection (old vs new firmware command set) is in `protocol_details.dialect_selection`.

services.name: FOREO Peach Command Service (service UUID hypothesized)
services.notes: CONTAINING SERVICE NOT PINNED ON HARDWARE. The app never hard-codes the service: it enumerates the discovered GATT table and selects characteristics by UUID. FFF1 is very likely under service FFF0 (the usual Telink arrangement), but no capture confirms it — clients MUST locate characteristics by enumeration, not by this service UUID. All command traffic is raw `opcode || payload` with no header, length or checksum; queries are written and then answered by READING FFF1 back. A read-back starting with FF FF FF FF means the device was busy — the app retries up to 5 times. Every write is verified by the same read-back.

security_access.description: Handshake: 01 A1 followed by the last three bytes of the device's own BLE MAC (printed order m0..m5; send m3 m4 m5).

mac3.description: Byte 3 of the device BLE MAC (4th printed octet).

mac4.description: Byte 4 of the device BLE MAC.

mac5.description: Byte 5 of the device BLE MAC (last octet).

characteristics.name: Security access
characteristics.notes: Session handshake, written once after EVERY service discovery; the device does not answer other commands before it. The stock app retries the write up to 3 times.

activate.description: Unlock a locked unit: 01 02 followed by the 8-byte chipId derived from the device's BLE MAC (keyless permutation, fully offline — see `protocol_details.activation`).

chip_id.description: 8-byte chipId = keyless nibble permutation of the 6-byte BLE MAC; algorithm and test vectors in protocol_details.activation.

characteristics.name: Activate (unlock/register)
characteristics.notes: Read first: a value whose first byte is 00 means the device is still locked. The unlock write is idempotent — the stock app re-runs the whole activation on every connect. chipId derivation is under `protocol_details.activation` with test vectors. (Other FOREO models use an older variant — 01 01 <ASCII serial> to this same characteristic; the Peach family uses the chip-id variant.)

characteristics.name: Wake-up
characteristics.notes: Read after activation; unless the value starts with 01, write 01 to enable wake-up.

characteristics.name: Serial number
characteristics.notes: Format not pinned beyond being read by the app.

characteristics.name: Chip ID
characteristics.notes: Distinct from the MAC-derived chipId written to 0A20 — this is a device-reported identifier the app reads.

characteristics.name: Skin-sensor / accelerometer polling
characteristics.notes: Polled during calibration. Response layout not recovered.

characteristics.name: OTA trigger
characteristics.notes: Reboots the device into OTA mode, after which the TI OAD service below takes over. Payload not recovered; whether the current app can OTA a Peach at all is unconfirmed — see `remaining_unknowns`.

services.name: FOREO Security/Activation characteristics (containing service unknown — stand-in UUID)
services.notes: CONTAINING SERVICE UUID UNKNOWN — this entry's UUID is a stand-in equal to the activation characteristic's. The app resolves every one of these characteristics by UUID from the discovered GATT table, so clients MUST do the same and MUST NOT match this entry as a service. All are 16-bit UUIDs on the standard base.

services.name: Battery Service
services.notes: Standard battery service; exposed even though the unit is mains-powered.

services.name: Device Information Service
services.notes: Standard DIS. SW revision (2A28) is read at every connect and selects the old/new command dialect (see protocol_details.dialect_selection).

services.name: TI OAD (Over-the-Air Download)
services.notes: Present in the app for firmware update after the 0A08 OTA-trigger reboot, with image characteristics …ffc1/…ffc2. No transfer flow was traced and no characteristics are documented — whether app 4.4.1 can actually OTA a Peach is unconfirmed, so no layout is claimed here. See `remaining_unknowns`.

services.name: Legacy Telink service (declared, apparently unused)
services.notes: Declared in the app but no use of any of its characteristics was found in 4.4.1 — listed so an implementer does not wait for traffic that never comes. No characteristics documented because none are used.
